name: Severin
label: Dischord
lede: Alec Bourgeois and Eugene Bogan came home from college, got Gray Matter's Mark Haggerty and Swiz's Alex Daniels, and in four years made one album and a run of singles for Superbad and Dischord. Dischord calls the sound melodic and chaotic.

eras.title: Bethesda kids, grown up
eras.text: Bourgeois and Bogan had been around the Bethesda punk scene since 1981. After college they started Severin, and it took a year and a few line-up changes to settle.

years.h: Two Bethesda thrashers come home from college and start Severin
years.p: Alec Bourgeois (guitar, vocals) and Eugene Bogan (bass) begin Severin in winter 1989. Dischord says the line-up changed several times before it held.
years.xp:
Superbad Records traces both to the "B-town thrashers," a crew of Walt Whitman and BCC high schoolers who started going to DC punk and art shows in 1981.

The early Severin line-ups included Joe Lally, Christina Billotte and Elio Mariani, before Haggerty and Daniels arrived in 1990.

years.cap: Severin: Bourgeois, Bogan, Haggerty and Daniels, early 1990s
years.h: Mark Haggerty of Gray Matter and Alex Daniels of Swiz fill out the band
years.p: [[Mark Haggerty|235b9917-3f4c-4670-ade3-d94f8e45a044]] takes second guitar and [[Alex Daniels|13781ee5-d298-48ae-a8a0-8478969142c8]] the drums, coming from [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]]. That line-up stays until the end.

eras.title: Melodic and chaotic
eras.text: Dischord's own phrase for Severin is melodic and chaotic. The band played dc space and the 9:30 Club, a bridge between DC's punk and indie-pop scenes, and toured in between records.

years.cap: Severin live at dc space, Washington, DC, early 1990s
yt: Fire and Sand / People Are Wrong, full single
years.h: Severin's first 7" pairs Fire and Sand with People Are Wrong
years.p: Dischord No. 57.5, co-released with Superbad Records. The same two songs later open and close the album Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust.

years.h: Haggerty's old band and his new one share a 7"
years.p: Dischord No. 68.72 puts [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]] and Severin back to back, with Mark Haggerty in both.

years.h: Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust is the one Severin album
years.p: Dischord No. 72, recorded at WGNS and produced by [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] with the band. Turner sang in Gray Matter.
years.xp:
Eleven songs, opening with Fire and Sand and closing with People Are Wrong, with Catholic Girl and Speaking Oyster in between.

The CD adds the songs from the Smash Hits 7" plus one more track.
play: Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust

years.h: The Smash Hits 7" adds more songs, which land on the CD
years.p: Dischord No. 72.5, another Superbad and Dischord single. Its songs are added to the CD of Acid to Ashes and Rust to Dust.

years.h: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, November 29, 1992
yt: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg PA, November 29, 1992

eras.title: A last single on Sub Pop
eras.text: The final year brought the Upside Down double single and Waste of Time on Seattle's Sub Pop. By fall the band had stopped.

years.h: Upside Down puts two records in one sleeve
years.p: Dischord No. 92.5, the last of Severin's Superbad singles.

years.h: Waste of Time is the one Severin 7" not on Superbad or Dischord
years.p: The band's fourth single comes out on Sub Pop in Seattle.

yt: Live at Decibels, Mechanicsburg, PA, Nov 29, 1992
years.h: Severin stops in the fall of 1993
years.p: Dischord dates the run from winter 1989 to fall 1993, after regional and national touring. One full set survives from Decibels in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania.
years.xp: The surviving set is a 44-minute VHS-C tape from November 29, 1992, posted by Erich's Archive.

eras.title: Dusters, Diamine and a Swiz reunion
eras.text: Bourgeois made a second life on Dischord with Capitol City Dusters. Daniels became a journalist and went back behind the Swiz kit.

years.h: Bourgeois turns up fronting Capitol City Dusters
years.p: The Severin singer leads Capitol City Dusters, another Dischord band, from 1995 to 2003. Haggerty drops in and out of Gray Matter from Baltimore; Bogan lives in Ontario.
years.xp: Dischord dates the Dusters from 1996; Superbad Records says 1995 to 2003.

years.h: Daniels drums with Swiz again while Bourgeois debuts Diamine
years.p: Alex Daniels, now a journalist near Washington, DC, plays the Positive Force 40th anniversary show with [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]]. Bourgeois's band Diamine puts out its debut album in May.
